title: The Crooked Wolf
premise: Marguerite Dravenmoor, a cartographer who maps realms that exist only in rumor, serves the Guild of Impossible Things by keeping its ledgers — records of bargains, doors, and debts. When a dying stranger presses a bloodstained map into her hands, she discovers it depicts Vellharrow, a country erased from every record she keeps, including her own memory of having been born there. Hunted by the Guild's enforcers and guided by the map's shifting ink, Marguerite and the stranger's surviving companion must reach the Crooked Wolf — the last standing door out of Vellharrow — before the country finishes forgetting itself and takes them with it. In the end, Marguerite learns she is the one who signed the order to erase Vellharrow to save the Guild, and she must choose between restoring her stolen identity or sacrificing both name and nation to keep the door open for those still trapped inside.
about_author: R. M. Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging maps of places that no longer appear in any atlas. They write from a house built on the site of a demolished railway station, which they insist still smells faintly of coal.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Marguerite Dravenmoor closes the Guild's accounts at dusk, noting an entry for a door sold twice. Her POV establishes her precision, loneliness, and quiet pride in knowing where everything is written. Emotional beat: controlled contentment about to crack.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Weighing House
chapters.summary: A bleeding man stumbles into the Guild's weighing house asking for 'the cartographer who remembers.' Marguerite insists she remembers nothing unusual. His POV briefly shows he recognizes her face. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Ink That Won't Dry
chapters.summary: The stranger presses a folded map into Marguerite's hands; the ink moves like living things. He dies whispering the word 'Vellharrow,' which appears nowhere in any ledger. Marguerite's POV. Emotional beat: vertigo of encountering the unmappable.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Omit
chapters.summary: Marguerite searches the archives and finds pages razored out — cut by a hand steady as her own. First-person doubt begins. Emotional beat: the horror of suspecting yourself.

chapters.title: The Guild Summons
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane questions Marguerite about the dead man, gentle and menacing. She lies for the first time in her career. His POV alternates. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by a single lie.

chapters.title: The Companion in the Rain
chapters.summary: Tobias Fenwick, the stranger's friend, finds Marguerite and demands the map. She refuses; they form a wary alliance. Dual POV. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Reading the Moving Map
chapters.summary: The map redraws itself nightly, showing roads that only exist while watched. Marguerite realizes it is navigating toward something. Her POV. Emotional beat: reluctant wonder rekindling her old love of cartography.

chapters.title: Enforcers at the Door
chapters.summary: Guild enforcers raid Marguerite's rooms. She and Tobias escape through the ledgers' own logic — a door recorded but never built. Tobias's POV. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Road Out of the Atlas
chapters.summary: They travel beyond mapped territory, where geography grows provisional. Marguerite experiences déjà vu of landscapes she shouldn't know. Her POV. Emotional beat: homesickness for a home she can't name.

chapters.title: Vellharrow
chapters.summary: They cross an unmarked border into a country that exists stubbornly, wrongly, alive. Marguerite reads street signs in a language she understands without translating. Her POV. Emotional beat: grief arriving before explanation.

chapters.title: The Town That Remembers Her
chapters.summary: In the town of Ashenwell, innkeepers greet Marguerite by a different name: Margo Vale. Tobias watches her deny it. His POV. Emotional beat: trust cracking under evidence.

chapters.title: Margo Vale's Room
chapters.summary: They find a boarding room preserved exactly as someone left it — with Marguerite's handwriting on unfinished maps of Vellharrow. Her POV, fractured. Emotional beat: identity beginning to split.

chapters.title: The Forgetting Wind
chapters.summary: A wind sweeps the countryside; afterward, a village has lost its river, then its name. The country is being unwritten. Tobias's POV. Emotional beat: urgency made visible.

chapters.title: Corvane's Version
chapters.summary: Interlude: Corvane briefs the Guild council, revealing Vellharrow was scheduled for erasure decades ago — and that the cartographer who drew its boundaries was their finest apprentice. His POV. Emotional beat: cold institutional certainty.

chapters.title: The Church of Recorded Names
chapters.summary: In Ashenwell's archive-church, a blind priestess keeps names alive by recitation. She tells Marguerite that some people sell memories to survive erasure. Marguerite's POV. Emotional beat: temptation of comfortable ignorance.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Tollbridge
chapters.summary: A toll-keeper demands payment in memories. Tobias offers his childhood; Marguerite stops him, offering a secret of her own instead — though she doesn't yet know what she paid. Dual POV. Emotional beat: sacrifice without understanding.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Paid
chapters.summary: Fragments surface: a signing desk, wax seals, an order bearing her signature. She confronts Tobias, who admits he knew who she was all along. Her POV. Emotional beat: betrayal compounding self-betrayal.

chapters.title: The Crooked Wolf Legend
chapters.summary: The priestess tells the tale of the Crooked Wolf: not a beast but a door, bent because it was forced open once before, guarded by whatever remains of the country's will. Tobias's POV. Emotional beat: myth becoming itinerary.

chapters.title: Pursuit on the Salt Flats
chapters.summary: Guild enforcers catch them on the salt flats; a chase across terrain that rearranges itself. Marguerite uses her cartographer's instinct to outrun them. Her POV. Emotional beat: competence as salvation.

chapters.title: Prisoner of the Guild
chapters.summary: Captured anyway, Marguerite is brought before Corvane, who offers truth as bait: she drew Vellharrow's borders, and she voted for its erasure to save the Guild from a war it would have lost. His POV and hers. Emotional beat: the floor giving way.

chapters.title: Why She Signed
chapters.summary: Corvane returns her sealed memories. Marguerite relives choosing erasure — and choosing to keep one copy of the country hidden inside a moving map. Her POV. Emotional beat: guilt reframed as buried heroism.

chapters.title: Escape From the Ledger Room
chapters.summary: Marguerite turns the Guild's records against itself, editing her own detention into contradiction, and walks free. Tobias waits outside, having chosen to believe her. Dual POV. Emotional beat: reconciliation through action.

chapters.title: The Country Fights Back
chapters.summary: Vellharrow itself begins resisting erasure — roads loop, storms defend passes. The land seems to recognize Marguerite's return. Her POV. Emotional beat: awe and responsibility entwined.

chapters.title: The Second Cartographer
chapters.summary: They discover another survivor: Ilsa, the stranger's sister, who has spent years keeping villages named by force of habit and chalk. Tobias's POV. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: Assembly at Ashenwell
chapters.summary: Survivors gather; Marguerite confesses publicly what she did. Some curse her; the priestess argues a penitent cartographer may be their only key. Marguerite's POV. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Map's True Purpose
chapters.summary: Marguerite deciphers her younger self's cipher: the moving map isn't a way out — it's the country's backup, waiting for someone to choose restoration over escape. Her POV. Emotional beat: the plan inverting.

chapters.title: Corvane Marches
chapters.summary: Corvane leads enforcers into Vellharrow to finish the erasure personally, fearing restored borders will resurrect the old war. His POV. Emotional beat: antagonist conviction that almost convinces.

chapters.title: The Road to the Wolf
chapters.summary: Marguerite, Tobias, and Ilsa race for the Crooked Wolf door through a landscape actively forgetting. A village they saved vanishes behind them. Tobias's POV. Emotional beat: running out of country.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Choice
chapters.summary: Wounded, Ilsa stays behind to hold a pass by reciting names until the wind takes even hers. Her POV, final entry. Emotional beat: martyrdom as authorship.

chapters.title: The Door Bent Twice
chapters.summary: They reach the Crooked Wolf: a door grown crooked from being opened against its nature. It asks a price — the true name of the one who opens it. Marguerite's POV. Emotional beat: threshold terror.

chapters.title: Which Name to Give
chapters.summary: Marguerite holds two names: Dravenmoor, earned; Vale, original. Giving either means losing the other forever. Dialogue with the door, her POV. Emotional beat: identity distilled to a single choice.

chapters.title: Corvane at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Corvane arrives; instead of fighting, he begs her to close the door and let the past stay dead, showing her the war's cost in Guild dead. His POV. Emotional beat: sympathy for the devil's arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Opening
chapters.summary: Marguerite gives the door neither name but the country's own — speaking Vellharrow back into itself. The door straightens. Climax begins. Her POV. Emotional beat: transcendence through renunciation.

chapters.title: The Country Remembers Itself
chapters.summary: Erased rivers, towns, and people flood back; the wind reverses. Corvane's enforcers are caught in the restoration — some saved, some unmade. Tobias's POV. Emotional beat: resurrection with casualties.

chapters.title: Confrontation on the Straightened Door
chapters.summary: Corvane and Marguerite fight not with weapons but with records — each citing ledgers, claims, histories. She wins by admitting her crime aloud, making it undeniable and therefore unfalsifiable. Her POV. Emotional beat: truth as weapon.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Ledger Entry
chapters.summary: Defeated, Corvane writes his own resignation into the Guild ledger and walks into Vellharrow as a private man. His POV, final entry. Emotional beat: dignity in surrender.

chapters.title: Cartographer of a Restored Country
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Marguerite surveys Vellharrow properly, drawing it onto real maps at last. Tobias chooses to stay; she must choose too. Her POV. Emotional beat: peace offered, not yet accepted.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Hand
chapters.summary: Marguerite signs the new atlas 'Margo Vale Dravenmoor' — refusing the door's either/or, since the country now holds both. Her POV. Emotional beat: synthesis of divided self.

chapters.title: The Last Unmapped Place
chapters.summary: Marguerite leaves one region blank on every map, labeled only 'still deciding.' She departs through the Crooked Wolf, now a gate between worlds, carrying blank paper. Her POV. Emotional beat: bittersweet departure.

chapters.title: Ledger Closed, Ledger Open
chapters.summary: Epilogue: in the Guild hall, a new apprentice finds an unsigned map of a country that officially never existed — and feels inexplicably homesick. Distant third person. Emotional beat: story becoming legend, wound becoming invitation.
